dimensions.detail: The advertised capabilities fit the stated purpose: task coordination, dashboard views, Claude session visibility, GitHub issue sync, webhook monitoring, CLI commands, and agent file editing.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The instructions are user-directed documentation and say nothing executes automatically; some referenced features involve sensitive local files, tokens, automatic task creation, and reset commands, so users should review the linked application before running it.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Install metadata contains links only, not executable shell install steps. Setup commands such as git clone, npm install, and server startup appear as documentation for user-run self-hosting.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Node.js and Git are proportionate for a self-hosted web dashboard, but the resulting app may read local Claude session data, use GitHub credentials, connect to MissionDeck cloud, and expose a local dashboard if configured that way.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Persistence is disclosed and purpose-aligned: .mission-control data files, optional PM2/systemd service setup, localStorage UI state, and persistent edits to agent SOUL/MEMORY/IDENTITY files with stated auto-backup.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.findings:
[SQP-2] expected: Claude session tracking is explicitly described, including the ~/.claude/projects/ path, 60-second discovery, and surfaced fields; this is privacy-sensitive but disclosed and central to the dashboard purpose.
[SQP-2] expected: GitHub issue sync and use of GITHUB_TOKEN/GITHUB_REPO are disclosed; users should still use least-privilege tokens and understand that sync talks to GitHub.
[SQP-2] expected: The SOUL editor openly states that it can view and edit SOUL.md, MEMORY.md, and IDENTITY.md in the browser and creates backups; high impact, but not hidden or unrelated.
[SQP-2] expected: Telegram auto-routing clearly says mentioned bot messages automatically create task cards with no manual logging; users should enable it only for trusted channels.
[SQP-2] expected: The reset commands are destructive but scoped to .mission-control task data and presented under a reset section; the docs would be safer with backup warnings, but there is no automatic execution.
llm.guidance: Before installing or running the linked app, audit the GitHub code and dependencies, keep the dashboard local or protected, use least-privilege GitHub and MissionDeck credentials, avoid exposing the SOUL editor to untrusted users, and back up .mission-control before using reset commands.
llm.summary: This is a documentation-only skill for a self-hosted mission-control dashboard, with sensitive features disclosed but worth reviewing before use.
